text: Cold knock. I open with something about him (the dog) before any pitch, then name neighbors on his street so I'm the guy already working the block. Ending on a question gets him talking instead of closing the door.
He already has a provider, which most reps treat as a dead end. I welcome it, give Champion credit, and tee up a reason to keep listening: 2 things we do that they don't.
Price reveal. I explain the 30-day follow-up (breaking the egg cycle) right as the number lands, so $250 for the first quarter reads as 2 treatments instead of a high bill.
First price objection. I acknowledge it and move on without arguing. Then I pivot to his pavers and teach how ants nest under them, building value specific to his home before price comes back up.
"Not ready" is vague, so I ask what matters most. He names cost and his current price, and now I know the real objection and can solve that one directly.
RAC: resolve, ace, close. I drop the first service to $69, framed as a route deal for his street, then lock the quarterly rate in writing so he isn't worried about price creep.
Risk reversal. Free re-treats, a 100% guarantee, A+ BBB, and 4.7 on Google all lower the risk of switching, which matters when he's comparing against a company he's happy with.
"Twice as much for no problems." Cutting price again would cheapen the offer, so I add value: a custom sunroom treatment every visit at no extra cost.
"Let me think about it." I lean on social proof (neighbors already on the route) and timing (heat in late May, a rainy season) to give him a reason to decide today.
He asks for more off. I hold the line at $69 and anchor to value instead of the competitor's price. Holding firm here is what makes the deal feel real.
The yes. He calls it a good pitch and still signs, a sign the trust held up all the way through.
Asking for payment right away, assumptive and low-key, so the yes turns into a real sale before the energy fades.
Setting expectations: service tonight, a text before the tech arrives, garage access. Clear next steps cut down on cancellations.
